channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Officials punished for violating construction norms in Karakol
item.description: Violations of construction norms were identified in Karakol, according to the Ministry of Construction. An object on Kadyrov Street was used as a guest house despite being designated for individual housing. Construction work was also carried out on Koenkosov Street without proper permits. Administrative measures were taken against responsible individuals.

item.title: Uzbekistan enacts new law to protect victims of violence and oppression
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a law enhancing social services for victims of violence and oppression. The legislation aims to improve protection mechanisms for women and children, remove administrative barriers to accessing aid, and expand state-funded legal assistance. It strengthens legal guarantees for victims' rights.

item.title: Uzbek President Attends First Central Asia-Korea Business Summit in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea Business Summit in Seoul. Leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and South Korea also attended. Mirziyoyev proposed building cooperation on mutual complementarity, highlighting Central Asia's potential for Korean companies.

item.title: S7 Airlines Resumes Direct Flights Between Moscow and Urgench
item.description: S7 Airlines has resumed direct flights between Moscow and Urgench starting September 15. Flights will operate twice weekly on Airbus A320 aircraft. The resumption aims to restore air connectivity to Urgench, a key tourist and cultural center in Uzbekistan and gateway to Khiva.

item.title: Belarus Frees 25 Political Prisoners in Exchange for US Sanctions Relief
item.description: Belarus released 25 political prisoners following negotiations with a US special envoy. In return, the US will lift sanctions on two Belarusian enterprises, Lakokraska and Bellesbumprom. Both sides will continue working on remaining issues, with further releases and sanctions relief contingent on full resolution. The freed individuals have reportedly left Belarus for Lithuania.

item.title: Bishkek Honors Soldiers Who Died Defending Kyrgyzstan's State Border
item.description: An event was held in Bishkek to commemorate soldiers who heroically died defending Kyrgyzstan's state border. The ceremony was attended by the Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs, a Member of Parliament, and commanders of the Internal Troops. Participants honored the memory and valor of the fallen servicemen.

item.title: Uzbek-Korean Cooperation Elevates to Strategic Partnership Level
item.description: Cooperation between Uzbekistan and the Republic of Korea is advancing to a new level of strategic interaction. This transformation focuses on integrating technologies, finance, science, human capital, and production into a unified economic chain. Key areas include industrial cooperation, deep processing of copper, and developing high-value sectors like robotics and pharmaceuticals.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia sign memorandum on enforcement cooperation
item.description: Representatives from Serbia's Chamber of Public Enforcement Officers visited Uzbekistan to strengthen cooperation in enforcement matters. The visit included meetings and an exchange of experiences, culminating in the signing of a memorandum of cooperation between the enforcement bureaus of both countries.

item.title: Uzbek President concludes state visit to South Korea
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has concluded his state visit to the Republic of Korea. He and his wife were seen off at the airport by the South Korean Minister of Interior and Safety, along with other officials.

item.title: Authorities Explain Fire in High-Rise Building in Dushanbe
item.description: Fire services explained a fire that occurred on September 14-15 in a high-rise construction in Dushanbe. The fire, which started around 02:38 on September 15, affected one apartment over 15 square meters. A short circuit in air conditioner electrical equipment was identified as the cause.

item.title: Uzbekistan to improve medical and pharmaceutical кадров training system from 2027/2028
item.description: Uzbekistan will fundamentally improve its medical and pharmaceutical кадров training system. Starting the 2027/2028 academic year, the Ministry of Health will approve state order parameters for bachelor's degrees in medicine. Training will be based on current and future needs, considering regional demands and staff shortages.

item.title: Russia's LDPR Proposes 5% Tax on Migrant Money Transfers Abroad
item.description: Russia's Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR) has proposed a mandatory 5% tax on money transfers sent abroad by foreign citizens. The proposal, sent to the Finance Minister, suggests banks automatically deduct the fee and send it to the federal budget. LDPR claims this would boost the Russian economy and help cover costs associated with foreign citizens in Russia.

item.title: Russia's LDPR proposes 5% tax on migrant money transfers abroad
item.description: Russia's Liberal Democratic Party (LDPR) has proposed a mandatory 5% tax on money transfers sent abroad by foreign citizens. The party suggests banks automatically deduct this fee and transfer it to the federal budget, arguing funds earned in Russia should benefit the Russian economy. This proposal aims to increase federal revenue and cover costs associated with foreign citizens in Russia.

item.title: Uzbek President Addresses First Central Asia-South Korea Summit in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev spoke at the first Central Asia-South Korea summit in Seoul, praising the host nation's dynamic development. He highlighted South Korea's early recognition of Central Asia's partnership potential and expressed appreciation for its contributions to industrialization and infrastructure modernization in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New List of State Assets for Privatization
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved a new list of major state assets to be privatized, following a presidential decree to reduce state participation in the economy. The list includes stakes in financial institutions, industrial, transport, and trade enterprises. New regulations for selling state assets and land plots via auction have also been introduced.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Five Cooperation Areas at Central Asia-South Korea Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the first Central Asia-South Korea summit in Seoul, proposing cooperation in five strategic areas. Discussions focused on expanding mutually beneficial collaboration in security, practical cooperation, and humanitarian exchanges. The summit included leaders from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan.

item.title: Damaged building collapses in Gaza war, killing 20 people
item.description: A building damaged by the war collapsed in Gaza, resulting in 20 fatalities. Witnesses reported hearing children crying for help from beneath the rubble. Hundreds of people are feared to be trapped under the debris.

item.title: Kazakhstan proposes new method for calculating damage from tree felling
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a new approach to calculating damages for illegal tree and shrub destruction. A deputy suggested that the assessment should consider factors beyond just the number of plants, including species' conservation status and restoration costs.

item.title: Kazakhstan proposes new method for calculating damage from tree felling
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a new approach to calculating damages for illegal tree and shrub destruction. A deputy suggested that assessments should consider factors beyond just the number of plants, including species rarity, recovery potential, and ecological significance.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes integrating Central Asia and South Korean potential
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea business summit, proposing cooperation based on complementary potential. He highlighted Central Asia's market of over 80 million people and its resources. Uzbekistan's mineral resources are valued at $3 trillion, with 120 projects planned in critical minerals.

item.title: Uzbekistan's state budget revenues increased by nearly 44% in six months
item.description: Uzbekistan's state budget revenues grew by almost 44% in the first six months of the year. The Minister of Economy and Finance stated that 72% of budget revenues came from taxes and 20% from duties, with the largest portion of expenditures allocated to education.

item.title: Osh police search markets and car washes for children not attending school
item.description: Police in Osh, Kyrgyzstan, are conducting raids in markets, train stations, and car washes to identify minors who are not attending school, are unsupervised, or are in difficult life situations. The operation, part of the "Salam, Mektep!" campaign, aims to ensure child safety, their right to education, and prevent juvenile delinquency.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explores AI's Role in Governance and Legal Challenges
item.description: Uzbekistan is integrating Artificial Intelligence into state functions, including citizen services and data analysis, as outlined in its AI Development Strategy until 2030. The move aims to reduce bureaucracy and improve public services. However, legal experts raise concerns about AI's impact on human rights and accountability for algorithmic errors.

item.title: Zelensky claims Russian drones entered Moldova twice while his plane was there
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russian drones twice entered Moldova's airspace while his presidential aircraft was present. He reported this occurred during his flight to Moldova and again on his return journey. Zelensky believes Russia aims to intimidate and demonstrate its power, noting a lack of response to such actions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to implement supervisory technologies in banking sector by 2031
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank has approved a concept and roadmap for developing supervisory technologies (SupTech) from 2026 to 2031. The program aims to automate regulatory processes using AI, machine learning, and big data. It will align supervisory practices with global digital standards, focusing on simplifying licensing and combating financial crime.

item.title: Bishkek mayor urged to use public transport to improve city comfort
item.description: An activist suggested Bishkek's mayor should use public transport to demonstrate how to make the city comfortable for everyone. The activist linked transport and environmental issues to decision-making processes and advocated for mayoral elections and citizen participation in urban policy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan schools face textbook shortage despite state funding
item.description: Kyrgyz schools are experiencing a significant shortage of textbooks, forcing parents to purchase them privately. Despite substantial state funding allocated for textbook printing by the state-owned "Uchkun" enterprise, books are appearing on markets at inflated prices, raising concerns about distribution and accountability.

item.title: Navoiy Region to Adopt Egyptian Experience in Desert Land Reclamation
item.description: Navoiy Region's delegation visited Egypt to discuss water resource management and desert land reclamation. The region plans to adopt Egypt's experience in utilizing desert areas and modern irrigation technologies, particularly for the Kyzylkum desert. Discussions included hydrogeological and economic assessments of potential desert sites.

item.title: Uzbek President Invites South Korean Companies to Invest in Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev invited South Korean companies to invest in artificial intelligence projects in Karakalpakstan. He emphasized that AI could create at least $10 billion in added value for every country's economy within five years.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts Conference on Strengthening State Cooperation with Overseas Diasporas
item.description: A national conference on engaging Tajik diasporas and compatriots abroad as development partners was held in Dushanbe. Organized by the Ministry of Labor, Migration and Employment, the event aimed to foster dialogue and leverage the potential of diasporas for sustainable national development.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Invites Korean Business to Participate in Major Projects
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov invited Korean companies to participate in the construction of Kambaratinskaya HPP-1, the development of the 'Ala-Too Resort' and the creation of logistics centers along the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway. Kyrgyzstan is ready to support investors through a 'one-stop shop' principle.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sees decline in private housing construction for January-August
item.description: In January-August 2026, Kyrgyzstan commissioned 6,009 individual residential buildings totaling 822,900 square meters, with investments reaching 26.2 billion soms. Housing completions fell by 0.7 percent compared to the previous year. Bishkek saw a 28.7 percent increase, while Batken region grew by 25.6 percent. Jalal-Abad, Osh, Chui, Talas, and Issyk-Kul regions experienced declines.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes lifting ban on new airline registrations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering lifting the moratorium on registering and certifying new airlines. The State Agency for Civil Aviation developed a draft presidential decree, stating that the goals of the moratorium, imposed in November 2024, have been achieved. Checks on airlines operating outside Kyrgyzstan and those whose aircraft were not based domestically have been completed, with identified violations rectified.

item.title: Uzbekistan's economy grew 8.5% in first half of 2026, budget deficit at 0.7% of GDP
item.description: Uzbekistan's consolidated budget deficit was 0.7% of GDP in the first half of 2026. The economy grew 8.5%, driven by services, construction, industry, investment, and exports. Annual inflation stood at 6.4%.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes 'cooperation for rapid development' vision with Central Asia and South Korea
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed developing a long-term conceptual vision titled 'Central Asia - Republic of Korea: Cooperation for Rapid Development'. The initiative was put forward by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the first summit between the region's countries and South Korea in Seoul.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Customs Disrupt Synthetic Drug Smuggling Channel in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Northern Railway Customs and the Interior Ministry's anti-drug service have dismantled an illegal mephedrone smuggling operation in Bishkek. An 18-year-old woman was detained with a large quantity of the synthetic drug, which could have generated over 10 million soms.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Monthly Allowances for Medical Personnel Starting January 1
item.description: Starting January 1, certain medical professionals in Uzbekistan will receive monthly allowances based on their qualifications. Graduates of bachelor's programs will receive one minimum wage, master's graduates two, and family medicine specialists four.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Decline in Private Housing Construction in August
item.description: In January-August, Kyrgyzstan commissioned 6,009 private homes totaling 822,900 square meters, with investments reaching 26.2 billion soms. However, housing area put into operation decreased by 0.7% compared to the previous year, reversing a positive trend.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Imposes Six-Month Ban on Certain Construction Material Imports
item.description: The Kyrgyz government has implemented a temporary six-month ban on the import of specific construction materials. This measure aims to protect domestic producers, stabilize the internal market, and ensure national economic security against foreign competition.

item.title: Vietnamese ROX Group Considers Major Investment Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: Vietnam's ROX Group is exploring new investment projects in several regions of Uzbekistan, including Bukhara, Samarkand, and Jizzakh. In Bukhara, a project valued at $2 billion aims to construct modern real estate, residential areas, schools, and infrastructure on over 85 hectares, potentially creating 5,000-6,000 jobs and improving housing for over 50,000 citizens.
